application.name: Foundation Stereo
application.description: Learned stereo disparity and depth with holoscan-foundation-stereo's FoundationStereoOp and NVIDIA's Fast-FoundationStereo through TensorRT, from a rectified stereo pair and its ROS camera_info files: a synthetic scene checked against ground truth, or a recording checked against the camera's own depth, shown beside the left image on a HoloViz display. Its ci mode runs the module's stub model, checked against the CPU reference of the operator's chain.

changelog.1.0.0: Initial release: the holoscan-foundation-stereo demo, with calibration from ROS camera_info files, a synthetic source checked against ground truth, a recording player checked against the camera's depth and the depth's camera info, a stub-model ci mode, and a HoloViz display, on screen or offscreen.

hardware.name: NVIDIA GPU
hardware.description: A CUDA-capable GPU supported by the Holoscan SDK, with TensorRT 10.

data.name: C-Fast-FoundationStereo (NVIDIA Open Model Agreement)
data.description: For every mode but ci: the 480x736 ONNX model, which the module's prepare_model.py downloads into the data directory. Not part of this repository.

data.name: A rectified stereo recording
data.description: For the recording mode only: a folder named by FOUNDATION_STEREO_RECORDING with left.yaml and right.yaml (ROS camera_info files of a rectified pair), index.csv, 8-bit PGM left and right images and, to compare with the camera's depth, depth.yaml and 16-bit PGM depth images. Not part of this repository.

synthetic.description: Run the model on 300 frames of a rendered scene, check its disparity against the ground truth, and show it beside the left image when a display is available.

recording.description: Play a rectified stereo recording, named by FOUNDATION_STEREO_RECORDING, in real time, as from the camera, and show its disparity beside the left image. Add --camera-depth-scale with --run-args to compare the depth with the recording's own.

ci.description: Finite headless check that needs no download: 30 synthetic 640x480 frames through TensorRT with the module's stub model, each frame's disparity checked against the CPU reference of the operator's chain, and the display rendered offscreen and checked, the whole lossless graph on one worker.
